thesis_points: First publicly traded land banking REIT — 876 communities, 139,000 homesites, $8.4B homesite inventory under option

IROIC (9.5–10.3%) exceeds WACC; value-accretive at current P/BV of ~0.87x; book value grows as inventory expands
HOPP'R technology platform (centralized land analytics + deal execution) creates a moat difficult to replicate at scale
Consensus analyst: 'Land is land — unless there's a recession, no reason to trade at a discount to book'

key_debate.street: Lennar concentration risk (80% revenue); limited operating history makes walkaway risk difficult to price; housing macro headwinds

thesis_points: Quality over speed: replacing Forever 21 vacancies (~570K sqft) with experiential anchors at >2x legacy rents

thesis_points: Acquisition flywheel: relationship-driven bilateral sourcing → 8.16% cap rate, 18.7yr WALT, 2.2% annual bumps → 10.0% GAAP yield vs peers' 7–8%

risks: Competitive pressure on cap rates from PE/family offices

overview.narrative:
REITs traded mixed Wednesday with a clear defensive tilt, as healthcare names led the tape (avg +0.76%) while rate-sensitive sectors bore the brunt of selling. Towers fell hardest at -1.73%, with SBAC and AMT down 2.79% and 2.77% respectively, alongside retail (-1.57%) and net lease (-1.55%). The moves are consistent with a bear-steepening backdrop, punishing long-duration cash flows while rewarding near-term earnings visibility in healthcare. DHC surged 4.43% and VTR added 2.06%, suggesting continued rotation into senior housing fundamentals.

The healthcare-tower spread of +250bps on the day is notable and underscores a growing bifurcation between operationally driven stories and yield proxies. Industrial was essentially flat (-0.01%), masking a wide dispersion between LINE (+2.37%) and IIPR (-1.49%). Office remains idiosyncratic — HIW rallied 1.88% on Sunbelt re-leasing momentum while HPP dropped 2.85%, the session's worst performer, as West Coast vacancy concerns persist. Net lease weakness was broad-based, with even best-in-class WPC down 1.04%.

Positioning into Thursday should favor healthcare overweights and underweight duration-heavy towers and net lease until we see conviction on rate stabilization. Watch for any follow-through in DHC and VTR — momentum chasers could extend the healthcare bid. Industrial warrants neutral positioning given the lack of directional signal.
